children: German grocers Aldi and Lidl will need to be regulated under the same property rules in the U.K. as rivals like Tesco and Asda after the country's competition watchdog designated them as major supermarkets.

The Competition and Markets Authority said Thursday that Aldi, Lidl GB and Lidl NI will be covered by the same land agreement rules as the U.K.'s other large supermarkets, which seeks to prevent big retailers from making it harder for rivals to open nearby via their land agreements. The rules already apply to Asda, Co‑op, Marks and Spencer, Morrisons, Sainsbury's, Tesco and Waitrose, the CMA said.

The regulator said that once a retailer is designated under the rules, it can't include any prohibited restrictions in new land agreements--and the CMA can look at existing contracts at the request of landowners, developers, and rival.
The watchdog provisionally found in August that Aldi and Lidl could come under the scope of the rules.
Neither Aldi nor Lidl immediately responded to a request for comment.
